tasks.title: Main process: read each Pod's slash commands from the SDK, track commands_changed and the terminal set, and push the visible list on push:podCommands through the preload bridge
acceptance: C1. `src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts` declares `SlashCommandInfo` and `PodCommandsPush` with exactly the fields `contracts/slash-command-delivery.ts` gives them. It adds `podCommands: 'push:podCommands'` to `EVENT_CHANNELS`, and adds `podCommands(cb: (p: PodCommandsPush) => void): Unsubscribe` to `OrcastrateApi['on']`. Each new declaration carries a docblock that restates that contract's rules for it in place: the normalization rules on `SlashCommandInfo`, and snapshot-not-delta plus SDK order on `PodCommandsPush`. In the worktree, `grep -rn 'interface SlashCommandInfo' src` and `grep -rn 'interface PodCommandsPush' src` each print exactly one line, and that line is in `src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts`. At c218dd4, `git grep -n 'interface SlashCommandInfo' c218dd4 -- src` prints nothing.

C2. In `tests/unit/ipc/channels.test.ts`, the push-channel count test ('declares exactly 6 push channels', `:48-52` at c218dd4) asserts 7 and is renamed to match. The invoke-channel count test (`:41-46`) still asserts 22. Both pass.

C3 (preserved, newly covering the seventh channel). 'main emits every channel in EVENT_CHANNELS' (`channels.test.ts:131` at c218dd4) still iterates `Object.values(EVENT_CHANNELS)`, and it passes with `push:podCommands` among the emitted channels. That push is produced by opening a Pod whose fake SDK answers `supportedCommands`, not by calling a push sink directly.

C4. `src/preload/api.ts` adds `on.podCommands`, which subscribes to `EVENT_CHANNELS.podCommands` the same way as the other `on.*` members. The per-channel table in `src/preload/api.test.ts` (`:249-254` at c218dd4) gains the row `['podCommands', EVENT_CHANNELS.podCommands]`, and every test driven by that table passes for the new row.

C5. `PodRunner` in `src/shared/contracts/pod-runner.ts` gains the OPTIONAL member `supportedCommands?(): Promise<unknown>`. Its docblock says three things: it resolves the SDK's answer unvalidated, and the manager normalizes it; it resolves `null` when the SDK bridge offers no command surface; and it rejects with a `PodRunnerError` of code `NOT_RUNNING` before `start()` and after `stop()`. No other member of that file changes. `SdkSession` in `src/main/pod/sdk-bridge.ts` gains the optional `supportedCommands?(): Promise<unknown>`, and `defaultSdkBridge` implements it by calling the query's `supportedCommands()` (`sdk.d.ts:2506` in `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.235).
C6. `EXPECTED_MEMBERS` in `tests/unit/pod/contract.test.ts` (`:17-26` at c218dd4) gains `'supportedCommands'`, and 'exposes exactly the contract`s members and nothing more' passes.
C7. A new test shows that a started runner, whose fake SDK session's `supportedCommands` resolves an array `X`, resolves `X` itself (`toBe`).
C8. A new test shows that a started runner whose fake SDK session has no `supportedCommands` member resolves `null`.
C9. A new test shows that `supportedCommands()` on a runner that was never started rejects with a `PodRunnerError` whose `code` is `NOT_RUNNING`.
C10. A new test shows that `supportedCommands()` called after `stop()` rejects with a `PodRunnerError` whose `code` is `NOT_RUNNING`.

C11. A new test mocks `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` with `vi.mock`, the way `tests/unit/pod/fork-session.test.ts:16` does, so that `query()` returns an object whose `supportedCommands` resolves a sentinel array. The test shows that `defaultSdkBridge(...).supportedCommands?.()` resolves that same array (`toBe`), and that the mocked `supportedCommands` was called exactly once.

C12. `src/main/pod-manager/slash-commands.ts` exports `normalizeSlashCommands(value: unknown): SlashCommandInfo[]` and `SLASH_COMMANDS_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`, whose value is `10_000`. A new test shows that `null`, `undefined`, a plain object and a string each normalize to `[]`.

C13. A new test normalizes a five-entry input: valid `A`, `null`, `{ name: '' }`, `{ name: 7 }`, valid `B`. The output has exactly two entries, `A` then `B`, each with the four `SlashCommandInfo` fields.
C14. A new test shows that an entry with a valid `name` and a non-string `description` and `argumentHint` normalizes with both fields `''`.

C15. A new test shows two things about `aliases`. It becomes `[]` when it is absent or is not an array. When it is an array mixing strings and non-strings, it keeps only the string members, in their original order.

C16. A new test opens a Pod whose fake SDK answers `supportedCommands` with a two-entry list. Exactly one `push:podCommands` push follows, carrying `{ podId, commands }` with the normalized list. The fake's `supportedCommands` was called exactly once.
C17. A new test opens a Pod whose fake SDK's `supportedCommands` never settles. `openPod` resolves, the `podStatus` push with `status: 'idle'` is emitted, and no `push:podCommands` push is emitted.

C18 (backend discipline, Async: 'Every asynchronous operation crossing a process boundary carries a cancellation mechanism and a timeout'; the SDK's `supportedCommands()` takes no abort signal, so the timeout is the whole of what this task can give it). A new test runs C17's setup under `vi.useFakeTimers()` and advances the clock by `SLASH_COMMANDS_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`. The manager's injected logger then holds exactly one `warn` whose text contains the Pod id and the word `supportedCommands`, and no `push:podCommands` push has been emitted. The test reads no wall clock.

C19 (backend discipline, Logging: 'Log at boundaries and at decisions'; Error handling: 'Never swallow an error'). A new test makes the fake SDK's `supportedCommands` reject. The logger then holds exactly one `warn` containing the Pod id and `supportedCommands`, no `push:podCommands` push is emitted, and the Pod's stored status is still `'idle'`.

C20. A new test drives a `{ type: 'system', subtype: 'commands_changed', commands: [...] }` message through the fake SDK stream after C16's first push. A second `push:podCommands` push follows, carrying the normalized replacement list.

C21. A new test holds the initial read pending and drives a `commands_changed` message, after which one push follows. It then settles the initial read with a different list. No further `push:podCommands` push is emitted.
C22. A new test drives a `system`/`init` message with `terminal_slash_commands: ['doctor']`, then a catalog of `[a, doctor, b]`. The pushed list is `[a, b]`, in that order.
C23. A new test continues C22 with an `init` message that has no `terminal_slash_commands` field. A push follows carrying `[a, doctor, b]`.
C24. A new test pushes a catalog, then drives two `init` messages with identical `terminal_slash_commands`. The second `init` causes no `push:podCommands` push.
C25. A new test opens a Pod whose `supportedCommands` resolves `[]`. Exactly one `push:podCommands` push follows, and it carries `commands: []`.
C26. A new test opens a Pod whose fake SDK session has no `supportedCommands` member, then drives an `init` message carrying `terminal_slash_commands`. No `push:podCommands` push is emitted.

C27. A new test uses a runner object that has no `supportedCommands` member, like the inert runner at `src/renderer/src/__tests__/pod-stop.e2e.test.tsx:141-154` (c218dd4). `openPod` resolves, and no `push:podCommands` push is emitted.
C28. A new test closes the Pod while its initial read is pending, then settles the read with a non-empty list. No `push:podCommands` push is emitted, and the logger receives no `error`.
C29. A new test opens two Pods whose fake SDKs answer different lists. Each `push:podCommands` push carries its own Pod's `podId` and that Pod's list.

C30 (preserved, newly tested). A new test drives one `commands_changed` message and one `init` message through an open Pod. Each is still persisted as exactly one `system` event, with its own subtype, on the Matriarch lane, as at c218dd4: there, `lane-router.ts:426-428` emits one `system` event for every system message that is not `task_progress`.

C31. `src/main/pod-manager/pushes.ts` declares `podCommands(payload: PodCommandsPush): void` on `Pushes`, and `createPushes` implements it by sending on `EVENT_CHANNELS.podCommands`. The header at `pushes.ts:4` says 'five' at c218dd4, even though `EVENT_CHANNELS` held 6 then. After this task it either states 7 or states no number.

C32 (test discipline, Coverage: 'A test is shown able to fail'). For each of C16, C21, C22 and C28, the report names one defect injected at one named `file:line` in a non-test file this task owns. For each, it also names the narrowest `VT` command run under the injection and the failure it produced, and confirms the revert, checked before any broader command was run. Suggested defects: C16, no initial read; C21, no discard of a late read; C22, no terminal filter; C28, no disposed-session check.

C33. `VT` below is `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree>`, and every `VT` run's `RUN` line must name the worktree, not the main checkout. `VT tests/unit/pod tests/unit/pod-manager tests/unit/ipc src/preload` exits 0.
C34. `npm run typecheck:node` exits 0. T1 is the only task running in its window, so this program reads no half-written peer file.

C35. `grep -rnE '\.sir/|20261112-2120' <each file in this task's owns>`, run in the worktree, prints nothing. At c218dd4, `git grep -l -E '\.sir/|20261112-2120' c218dd4 -- src tests` prints nothing. The control is `grep -cE '\.sir/|20261112-2120' .sir/lessons.md` in the main checkout, which prints a non-zero count. Every new or edited docblock states the rule it relies on in place and cites no session artifact.

tasks.title: LaneRouter: render local slash-command output, and the result text of a turn that bypassed the model loop, as assistant text
acceptance: C40 (gap G1). A new test file, `tests/router/slash-command-output.test.ts`, ingests `{ type: 'system', subtype: 'local_command_output', content: 'Context: 12k tokens', uuid, session_id }` into a lanes-mode router. Exactly one event comes back. Its `type` is `'assistant_text'`, its `laneId` is the Matriarch's, its `payload` deep-equals `{ type: 'assistant_text', text: 'Context: 12k tokens' }`, and its `raw` is the ingested message itself (`toBe`). The SDK's own description of the message is 'Displayed as assistant-style text in the transcript' (`sdk.d.ts:4257-4259` in the main checkout's `node_modules`), and `assistant_text` is in the renderer's conversation set (`transcript-filter.ts:40-45` at c218dd4).
C41. The C40 message, ingested into an inline-mode router, yields exactly one `assistant_text` event on the Matriarch lane.

C42 (preserved, newly tested). A `local_command_output` message whose `content` is absent, `''`, or not a string yields exactly one `system` event with subtype `'local_command_output'`. That is what c218dd4 yields for it (`lane-router.ts:426-428`).

C43 (gap G2). A new test ingests a `result` with `subtype: 'success'`, `is_error: false`, no `terminal_reason`, and `result: "/theme isn't available in this environment."`, with no Matriarch `assistant_text` since the router was built. Exactly two events come back, in this order. First, an `assistant_text` on the Matriarch whose `text` is the `result` string and whose `raw` is the message. Second, the `system` event whose payload deep-equals `{ type: 'system', subtype: 'result:success', data: message }`, which is what c218dd4 produces for that message (`lane-router.ts:512-518`). This rests on the SDK: `TerminalReason` is documented 'Unset when the loop was bypassed (local slash command)' (`sdk.d.ts:7908-7911`).
C44. The C43 message with `terminal_reason: 'completed'` added yields only the `system` `result:success` event.

C45. The C43 message, ingested after an `assistant` message whose text block routes to the Matriarch, yields only the `system` `result:success` event. That Matriarch text is the half of the discriminator that keeps a CLI without `terminal_reason` from showing every reply twice.
C46. An `assistant` text block routed to a Calf lane, because its `parent_tool_use_id` names a dispatched Calf, does not suppress C43's `assistant_text`.
C47. A `local_command_output` with non-empty `content`, followed by C43's result, yields exactly one `assistant_text` across the two ingests, and it is the local output's.

C48. A test runs two turns. Turn 1 is a Matriarch text block and then a C43-shaped result. Turn 2 is a C43-shaped result with no text since turn 1's result. Turn 1 yields no extra `assistant_text`, and turn 2 yields one. So the suppression is reset at each `result`.
C49. A C43-shaped result whose `result` is `''` or is not a string yields only the `system` `result:success` event.
C50 (preserved, newly tested). A result with `is_error: true` and no `terminal_reason` yields exactly the one `error` event it yields at c218dd4 (`lane-router.ts:502-508`), and no `assistant_text`.

C51 (preserved, newly tested). A new test replays every file that `discoveredFixtureFiles()` (`tests/router/helpers.ts:103`) returns, and finds no `assistant_text` event whose `raw` has `type` `'result'` or `subtype` `'local_command_output'`. Every fixture result carries `terminal_reason`. `grep -h '"type":"result"' tests/fixtures/protocol/*.ndjson | grep -c '"terminal_reason":"completed"'` prints 6. `cat tests/fixtures/protocol/*.ndjson | grep -c '"type":"result"'` also prints 6.

C52. The docblocks on `routeSystem` and `routeResult` in `src/main/lane/lane-router.ts` state both mappings and both halves of the G2 discriminator in place. They name the SDK declarations they rest on, `SDKLocalCommandOutputMessage` and `TerminalReason`.
C53. No file is added under `src/main/lane/`. The purity suite's shipped-file list (`purity.test.ts:69`) and its import rule (`:83`, siblings and `../../shared/contracts/` only) pass unchanged.

C54 (test discipline, Coverage: 'A test is shown able to fail'). The report names two injections, each at one named `lane-router.ts` line: dropping the `terminal_reason` check, which must fail C44's test, and dropping the Matriarch-text check, which must fail C45's test. For each it gives the narrowest `VT` command run under the injection and the failure it produced, and confirms the revert, checked before any broader command was run.
C55. `VT` below is `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree>`, and every `VT` run's `RUN` line must name the worktree, not the main checkout. `VT tests/router src/main/lane` exits 0.
C56. `npm run typecheck:node` exits 0. T3 and T4 run beside this task, but they edit only `src/renderer/**`, which `tsconfig.node.json`'s `include` (`:2-10`) does not reach.

C57. `grep -rnE '\.sir/|20261112-2120' <each file in this task's owns>`, run in the worktree, prints nothing. At c218dd4, `git grep -l -E '\.sir/|20261112-2120' c218dd4 -- src tests` prints nothing. The control is `grep -cE '\.sir/|20261112-2120' .sir/lessons.md` in the main checkout, which prints a non-zero count. Every new or edited docblock states the rule it relies on in place and cites no session artifact.

tasks.title: Composer: slash-command suggestion list above the textarea, with prefix match on name or alias, at most five rows, and keyboard and pointer acceptance
acceptance: C80. `ComposerProps` in `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-view.ts` (`:325-334` at c218dd4) gains the required member `commands: readonly SlashCommandInfo[]`, imported from `@shared/contracts/ipc`, with a docblock that restates part B of `contracts/renderer-slash-commands.ts` in place. `onInterrupt`'s docblock gains the sentence 'Not called while the suggestion list is open: Esc then closes the list instead.' No other member changes.

C81. `src/renderer/src/composer/slash-suggestions.ts` exports a pure `matchSlashCommands(text: string, commands: readonly SlashCommandInfo[]): SlashCommandInfo[]`. A new test passes it `'/'` and seven commands and gets exactly the first five, in input order.
C82. A new test shows that `'/co'` returns exactly the commands whose `name` starts with `co`, in input order.
C83. A new test shows that `'/st'` returns a command named `usage` whose `aliases` include `stats`, and that it is the command object itself, not a copy renamed to the alias.
C84. A new test shows that each of `'compact'`, `' /compact'`, `'/compact now'` and `'/com\npact'` returns `[]`, given a list containing `compact`.
C85. A new test shows that `'/C'` returns `[]`, given a list containing `compact`: the match is case-sensitive.
C86. A new test shows that `'/zz'` returns `[]` when no name or alias starts with `zz`.

C87. A Composer test with `text: '/'` and three commands renders exactly one element with role `listbox` and a non-empty accessible name, holding exactly three `option` elements in `commands` order. Each option holds one element whose `textContent` is exactly `'/' + name` and another whose `textContent` is exactly `description`. Leaving out its `aria-hidden` descendants, the option's `textContent` is those two strings with nothing else between or around them except whitespace.
C88. A Composer test with eight matching commands renders exactly five `option` elements.

C89 (frontend discipline, Accessibility floor: 'Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard alone'; 'Semantic elements are used for their meaning'). While the list is open, the textarea has `aria-autocomplete='list'`, an `aria-controls` equal to the listbox's `id`, and an `aria-activedescendant` equal to the selected option's `id`. While the list is closed, the textarea has neither `aria-controls` nor `aria-activedescendant`.

C90 (frontend discipline, Accessibility floor: 'Color is never the only carrier of meaning'). The selected option has `aria-selected='true'`, and every other option has `aria-selected='false'`. The selected option also contains one `aria-hidden='true'` marker element that no other option contains.
C91. With the list open and row 0 selected, ArrowDown selects row 1.
C92. With the last row selected, ArrowDown selects row 0.
C93. With row 0 selected, ArrowUp selects the last row.
C94. When further typing changes the set of rows shown, for example from `'/'` to `'/c'`, row 0 is selected.
C95. With the list open and row 1 selected, Enter calls `onChange` once with `'/' + rows[1].name + ' '`. `onSend` is not called.
C96. With the list open, Tab calls `onChange` once with `'/' + rows[0].name + ' '`. `onSend` is not called, and `document.activeElement` is still the textarea.
C97. Accepting a row that matched only by an alias, as in C83, calls `onChange` with `'/usage '`, the canonical name.
C98. A `mousedown` on the second option calls `onChange` once with `'/' + rows[1].name + ' '`, and `document.activeElement` is still the textarea.
C99. With the list open, Escape removes the listbox from the DOM. Neither `onInterrupt` nor `onChange` is called.
C100. After C99's Escape, an edit whose new text still matches, such as `'/c'` to `'/co'`, shows the listbox again.
C101 (preserved, newly tested). With `text: '/compact now'`, so the list is closed, Enter calls `onSend` exactly once.
C102 (preserved, newly tested). With `text: '/zz'` and no matching command, so the list is closed, Enter calls `onSend` exactly once and Escape calls `onInterrupt` exactly once.
C103. With `text: '/'`, matching commands, and `disabled: true`, no `listbox` is rendered.
